title: dev-mentor stack registry entry
description: One file per stack. Describes how to detect the stack, which official agent skills exist for it, what those skills do not cover, and the mentor's stack-specific thresholds.

stack.description: Registry key. Must equal the filename without .json.

files.description: Manifest files whose presence suggests this stack. Forward slashes only.

markers.description: Substrings inside those files that confirm the stack. Needed when one manifest serves many stacks (package.json, pyproject.toml).

last_verified.description: Date a human last confirmed every id, install command and source_url in this file.

id.description: Skill repository in owner/repo form, or owner/repo#skill-name for a single skill inside a collection.

owner_kind.description: Who publishes it. The mentor states this when recommending, because a community skill carries different risk than a framework-team one.

skills.description: Individual skill names inside the repository, when it is a collection.

install.description: Verbatim install command. null when unverified; then needs_verification must be true.

needs_verification.description: true when any field here could not be confirmed against a primary source. The mentor must say so out loud before recommending it.

gap_map.description: What no official skill for this stack covers. Empty array is a claim that nothing is missing - justify it in notes.

layers.description: Either plain names (legacy) or objects carrying the judgment. Objects are strongly preferred: the name of a layer teaches nothing, but knowing what belongs in it and what it costs is the whole point.

cost.description: Confidence gained against maintenance and runtime paid.

signal_you_picked_wrong.description: The observable tell that a test is at the wrong layer - e.g. needing a widget pump to check a pure calculation.

commands.description: Keyed by purpose. The mentor runs the full-suite command before reporting any task complete.

rules.description: Checkable test rules for this stack, written verbatim into the project's CLAUDE.md. Stack-specific only: generic doctrine already lives in references/quality-gate.md and repeating it wastes the 150-line budget.

traps.description: Ways tests lie in THIS stack - the suite passes and the product is broken, or the suite fails for a reason unrelated to the change. This is the field a model is least likely to volunteer on its own.

what_not_to_test.description: Tests that cost maintenance and buy nothing in this stack. Naming these prevents the busywork a coverage target produces.

proportions.description: What the framework team says about the shape of the suite, attributed. The shape is the point; any number is illustration.

growth_thresholds.description: Stack-specific overrides of references/growth-signals.md. Every value states the number AND the unit so the threshold is auditable.

dead_code_risks.description: Patterns in this stack that look unreferenced but are not. Feeds mentor-clean's requires_human_review classification.

architecture.description: The architecture the framework team recommends, the named variants a senior would choose between, and the checkable rules the mentor writes into the project's CLAUDE.md. This is routing and judgment, not documentation: never explain what a pattern IS - record which variant this framework's team recommends, when to deviate, and what breaks if you choose wrong.

recommended_by.description: framework-team means the maintainers published it. Anything else the mentor must present as an opinion, not as doctrine.

optional.description: true when the framework team calls this layer optional. The mentor must not add an optional layer without an observed reason - that is the over-abstraction growth signal.

folder_strategy.description: The single most consequential structural choice, and the one teams get wrong once and pay for permanently.

variants.description: The real decision a senior makes. Each variant names when it wins and what it costs.

rules.description: Checkable invariants, written verbatim into the project's CLAUDE.md. Each must be verifiable by reading the code - 'domain imports no SDK' passes, 'keep it clean' does not.

component_library.description: When and how this stack organises shared UI, and at what point a component library stops being premature.

key_decisions.description: The decisions this stack FORCES on every new project - the ones with no framework default, where a silent pick is inherited for the life of the codebase. The mentor surfaces all of them at Step 0/1. This exists because an agent asking the right question is otherwise a matter of luck, and luck does not repeat.

why_it_is_forced.description: Why the framework does not decide it for you.

cost_of_getting_it_wrong.description: What it costs to change later. This is what makes it worth interrupting the user for.
